title: Clarinet
summary: Limits first: a fixed-pressure model, not a player. Blown at 1.8 kPa (18.4 cm H2O), under the 20 to 55 cm H2O measured on playing clarinettists (Fuks and Sundberg 1999); at 3.0 to 3.6 kPa a G4 test card has H8 to H12 30 to 32 dB over the recording's (23 at 1.8); nothing is posted there yet. One lumped reed mode on one slit lay; a printed 2-D contact law with a corner at its onset; a reed-noise law that is an extrapolation, so the notes are noisier than the recordings. No airway, lips or vibrato. The bore is the published 1981 Buffet Crampon Prestige of Taillard and Sanchez 2016 with its 24 tone holes, the open holes and bell sharing room air (Lefebvre, Scavone and Kergomard 2013), and the bore air follows Noreland's measured temperature profile. One barrel pull of 2.79 mm puts the 19 notes from D3 to G5 at -0.1 c from equal temperament on average, spread 10.0 c, solved without the printed tone-hole lengths; the 16 pages that carry them sound 0.6 to 13.4 c sharper than they do without them. Fingerings are Moers and Kergomard 2011 Table 2; Gb3 is inferred, Gb5 comes from two printed charts, and F6, from the same charts, speaks a low tone near 324 Hz, so its page stays recording-only. Eighteen pages (Ab3, Bb3, Bb4, C4, C5, D4, D5, Eb4, Eb5, F3, F4, F5, G3, G4, G5, Gb3, Gb4, Gb5) now also carry `open_hole_orifice N` (commit 43ad828c9; commit 453bf176c for G4 and Gb4, whose 14 and 13 open holes are above the old cap of 12 on the coupled holes), the quasi-steady orifice loss on all N of their open holes (N from 2 to 14) in place of the first open hole alone. Each was rendered beside a byte-identical control of its posted card and both were graded on the same library: 13 keep the count, Bb3, D5, G5, Gb5 lose one measure each, Gb4 loses two (pitch and harmonics-to-noise leave the ruler), none gains; the level falls by 0.0 to 5.5 dB, the tone moves by up to 4.4 c, and the render takes 4.3 to 6.4 times the CPU, a fixed cost of the render's build and not of the audio length. On A5 (N = 10) and Bb5 (N = 11) the row takes the note away (a low tone near 325 and 339 Hz in place of the note), so those two pages stay as they were, as do A4, Eb3 and D3, which have one open hole or none. The seven pages built before the reed's closure stop (Bb3, Eb3, Eb5, F3, G3, Gb3, Gb4) render the same bytes with the stop in, so the stop changes nothing on them.
physics_present: Air column from the published Buffet Crampon Prestige (1981) bore stations of Taillard and Sanchez 2016, Tableau 2, with all 24 tone holes as side branches at their published positions, minimal diameters and chimney heights, and the mouthpiece as an equivalent cylinder

Fingerings: the open set of each of the 21 normal fingerings from Moers and Kergomard 2011 Table 2, mapped to the Buffet's holes by hole index; Gb3 inferred from the table's rule (F3 with hole 4 also open), a fingering both the Woodwind Fingering Guide's Boehm chart and the UNSW 'Acoustics of the clarinet' diagram now show; Gb5 (written G#5) from those two printed charts
Open tone holes interact across the varying air field (the mutual-hole law, Lefebvre, Scavone and Kergomard 2013), with the open holes and the bell sharing the outside air

Bore air temperature profile measured by Noreland 2013, warm at the barrel and cool at the bell, as a continuous gas field of the exhaled-breath mixture (Coltman 1966, Nederveen 1969); room air outside
Reed: one lumped oscillator with mass, stiffness and damping at the embouchure of Chatziioannou and van Walstijn's Table 1 reed, with viscous slit flow at the reed

Reed contact with the lay: the law printed for this reed (Chatziioannou and van Walstijn, Acta Acustica united with Acustica 98(4), 629-639, 2012: K 6.263e6 N/m^2, exponent 2, onset at 0.16 mm of opening, no contact loss), on every note but Bb5, which keeps the engine's default contact because the printed law scored lower there
Reed noise: the duct-constriction law of Oldham and Ukpoho 1990, read at the reed slit with the total pressure drop and the Bernoulli speed
One barrel pull of 2.79 mm, solved once so the 19 notes from D3 to G5 average equal temperament
Blown at one fixed mouth pressure (1800 Pa), rising over 20 ms and released over 60 ms, with a tongue-contact row holding the reed on the lay while the pressure builds
Observer: the physical baffled outlet receiver, open holes and bell summed, room air around the bell and holes, ISO 9613 air absorption

On 15 of the 21 normal fingerings (D3, Ab3, C4, D4, Eb4, F4, G4, A4, Bb4, C5, D5, F5, G5, A5 and Bb5) and on Gb5, the printed tone-hole lengths (Lefebvre and Scavone 2012): thick-wall inner, matching and radiation lengths and the series inertance of every hole, open or closed. They move every one of those notes sharp, by 0.6 c (G4) to 13.4 c (D3)

Quasi-steady orifice loss at every open hole on 18 pages (`open_hole_orifice N`, commit 43ad828c9 and 453bf176c, N = the fingering's open holes: Ab3 4, Bb3 6, Bb4 2, C4 7, C5 3, D4 9, D5 4, Eb4 10, Eb5 5, F3 2, F4 12, F5 7, G3 3, G4 14, G5 8, Gb3 3, Gb4 13, Gb5 8): the sharp-edged separation law of the first-hole shunt (c_d 2.69, no threshold velocity), each hole's coefficient reading the gas at that hole, all N solved together through the bore; two stated approximations: each orifice sees its own uncoupled radiation load, not the coupled one of the interaction row, and the sound the holes radiate still comes from the linear network; the sharp-edge premise is not established for this Buffet (its hole edge radii are unmeasured). The other pages keep the first open hole alone
physics_missing: No player: no airway or vocal tract, no lips, no vibrato, no wall vibration; the lumped reed has one mode, with no reed continuum and no lip mass or damping

The contact law comes from a 2-D reed model, has a corner at its onset and is not a measured lay profile; its authors write that the fit is 'not accurate for near-closure displacements'. It is not matched to a recording

The reed-noise law was measured on dampers and orifice plates in a 300 mm duct at 10 to 25 m/s and does not fix the jet speed or pressure drop to use for a slit this small; that choice alone moves the source by up to 40 dB. The notes are noisier than the recordings (harmonics-to-noise 21.9 to 36.0 dB against 30.6 to 47.0 dB) and the level is not a prediction

The barrel pull sets the mean, not the spread: the 10.0 c spread about equal temperament is mostly this specimen's own playing pattern (Taillard and Sanchez 2016, Fig. 7, read from the figure, spreads 7 c over D3 to G5). The aim was equal temperament, not the recordings, and the pull is one step for every note

Pad height, undercuts, key geometry and the tone-hole edge radius are unmeasured for this Buffet, as are the mouthpiece interior (chamber, baffle, throat, lay) and the reed and mouthpiece the recordings used

The printed tone-hole length corrections (Lefebvre and Scavone 2012) on Eb3, F3, G3, Gb3, Bb3, Gb4 and Eb5: on each of those seven they lower the grader count by one, so those pages are rendered without them. On the 16 pages that carry them the count ties on 14 and rises on two, Bb5 (8 to 9 of 14) and Gb5 (11 to 12 of 15)
The recordings (University of Iowa Musical Instrument Samples) are another clarinet and player: there is no same-specimen comparison

Only the 21 normal fingerings of Moers and Kergomard 2011 Table 2 are printed there. Gb3 is inferred, not printed; Gb5 and F6 take their hole states from two other printed charts (UNSW; Woodwind Fingering Guide) by a mapping of drawn holes to the Buffet's that is a judgment, checked on 17 of the 17 decodable printed fingerings, and UNSW draws 'a Bb clarinet', not this Buffet. The card has no altissimo leak physics

F6 does not speak: with its printed fingering the card sounds a low tone near 324 Hz with a weak line at F6's own frequency 30 dB under it; the cause has not been isolated. The orifice row on every open hole brings a low tone of the same kind on A5 (N = 10: a 325 Hz line 8 dB over the note, 8 of 15 inside the ruler falling to 4) and Bb5 (N = 11: only a 339 Hz line, 9 of 14 falling to 3); a plane-wave transfer-matrix estimate of the cards' bores (a check of the author's, not the engine's operator) puts the first impedance peak at 340 Hz on A5, 355 Hz on Bb5 and 341 Hz on F6, 4.4 to 5.0 % above the three tones; in 0.9 s trials A5 loses the note from three coupled holes (the vent and the next two) and Bb5 from two (the vent and the next), and the level is flat beyond that; why the row hands the oscillation to the low tone is not shown

Every clarinet card ends in a flanged (infinite-baffle) radiation load, because the receiver used needs one; a real bell is unbaffled. At D3 the low-ka unflanged law raises the bore's impedance peaks by about 3 dB (2.8 dB, mean of the peaks between 0.6 and 1.9 kHz, re the playing peak); that law refuses above ka 1, about 1.9 kHz
The sharp-edge premise of the orifice row is not measured for this Buffet's holes (their edge radii are unmeasured), so the row is a consistency fix and not a calibration
blocked: F6 (written G6): the card speaks a low tone near 324 Hz instead of F6, so its page stays recording-only until the cause is found
